name: Mothwing
subtitle: the light-eating moths
story: The moths on Mothwing have wingspans like kites, and they live on light. Each night they lift the moonlight off the fields and carry it back up. Leave a candle in the window and they'll take that too, but they leave a little glowing dust on the sill, which lasts until morning.
hook: A planet for people who pretend to be out on Halloween.

odd_line: Missing: one candle. Found: a small pile of glowing dust.
rule: Candles left out after dark are considered a donation.
question: Would you leave a candle out?

beats.text:
Leave a candle out
and your moth will take it.

They're very polite about it.
They always leave the wick.

Everyone leaves one out.
Not Gordon.
He says he's not made of candles.

His moth sat on the roof all night,
looking in.

episode.end: Your moth is on the roof tonight.
episode.caption:
Mothwing has 19,000 people, two moons and a 36-hour day, so the nights run to eighteen hours and the moths are never short of work. They have wingspans like kites and live on light. Every night they lift the moonlight off the fields and carry it back up, and each one keeps the same round of windows all its life. A candle left on the sill after dark counts as a donation. They take the flame, leave the wick, and leave a little glowing dust that lasts until breakfast. Nobody sells nightlights. There'd be no point.

Nobody has ever been hurt by one. Several people have been made to feel terrible.

I left a torch out on my first night, to be helpful. I got it back. Switched off.

What does your family say they're not made of?

first_comment: Gordon would like it known that he is still not made of candles. He has ordered more.

short.title:
The moths here
eat moonlight.
short.sub:
Everyone leaves them a candle.
Except Gordon.

beats.text:
So his moth sat on the roof
all night, looking in.

short.end: Now Gordon leaves out a spare moon.
